page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, it features 4 physical cores with hyperthreading to deliver 8 dedicated virtual CPUs. The instance is configured with 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. It includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction support for AVX-512 and AES encryption. The instance does not include bundled local SSD storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady middle-tier performance across general application workloads. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 8292.45 and a Passmark memory score of 2329.07. Memory performance testing recorded uncached read speeds of 50.27 GB/sec and write speeds of 37.18 GB/sec. For application throughput, the server executed 7.12 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.9 GB/sec in static web serving tests. Multi-core performance in dense parallel tasks like Geekbench multi-core (4464.0) and bzip3 decompression (27.31 GB/sec) scored in lower percentiles relative to instances with higher physical core counts.

The n2-standard-8 provides resource density suited for standard software workloads requiring predictable CPU execution without credit limits. While lacking local NVMe disk arrays, its balanced memory capacity and dedicated virtual CPUs offer a cost-effective platform for enterprise web applications, microservice clusters, middle-tier databases, and build pipeline workers.
